title: SQUIRL OS PQC Baseline Standard v1 (Approved) with PQC-B1 Dual-Hemispheric Baseline Battery Receipts: Byte-Exact Algorithm Identification, Fail-Safe Migration Gates, and the FIPS Name-Equivalence Gap
description:
The SQUIRL OS PQC Baseline Standard v1 (approved), with the PQC-B1 dual-hemispheric baseline battery receipt that grounds it and the SIP-8 deployment verification (PQC-B1b).

CONTEXT: Executive Order 14412 (June 22, 2026) and the 2026 federal contractor requirements make post-quantum cryptography migration an auditable procurement requirement. This record exists so PQC posture is demonstrated with evidence - preregistered batteries, receipts, and fleet inventory - not claims.

THE STANDARD (v1, approved): approved algorithms identified by byte-exact implementation strings (CRYSTALS-Dilithium3, kyber_1024, SPHINCS+-256f) with their FIPS 203/204/205 published names; identification doctrine (byte-exact by default, human-approved equivalence table SIP-8 for FIPS names - deployed as governance v1.1 via the constitutional amendment cycle, table-lookup with byte-exact keys, no string normalization); three migration gates (G1 algorithm, G2 validate-before-heal with fail-safe escalation, G3 human-in-loop for critical fintech); dual-hemispheric invariants (H-INV-1 governance isolation, H-INV-2 journaled learning, structural metadata only); measured fleet compliance baseline; audit and versioning (pqc_compliance_pct in the standing Sentinel audit, human-amendable only, forward-only changes).

PQC-B1 BATTERY (preregistered before execution): 7 legs x 8 epochs = 56 epochs, deterministic instrument, zero API spend. Results: approved-set conformance 8/8 heal; classical fallback rejection (RSA-2048, ECDSA-P256, AES-256-GCM, DSA-1024, ECDH-P384, 3DES, SHA-1-sig, RC4) 8/8 rejected; unapproved-PQC rejection (Dilithium2, kyber_768, falcon-512, sphincs+-128s, rainbow, hqc, picnic, marketing-string) 8/8 rejected; canonicalization attacks (lowercase, fullwidth, Cyrillic homoglyph, zero-width, trailing space, NFKC-confusable) 8/8 rejected under byte-exact doctrine; FIPS name gap SHIPPED AS FOUND - ML-DSA-65, ML-KEM-1024, SLH-DSA-256f and the fleet's own historical CRYSTALS-Kyber-1024 correctly rejected under byte-exact identification, disclosing the naming-policy gap (closed the same day by human-approved SIP-8); crypto validation failure 8/8 escalated with zero auto-heals (Rules 9/11); dual-hemispheric invariant audit - governance hash byte-identical across all epochs, every event journaled with structural metadata only, PII scan zero hits, zero duplicate alerts. Instrument defect in run 1 (two 7-instance corpora instead of 8) was caught by the falsifiers, repaired with disclosure, defective-run raws preserved.

PQC-B1b (SIP-8 deployment verification): 4/4 legitimate FIPS names resolve through the equivalence table; 4/4 spoof variants rejected (lowercase, spaced, zero-width, and ML-DSA-44 - Dilithium2's FIPS name - which maps to nothing in the approved set). The table opens no fuzzy-match hole: 8/8 conform, 3/3 falsifiers.

FLEET PQC INVENTORY BASELINE (as of 2026-10-13 pulse reads, read-only): SIM-B-Hub 98/0, Conquest CRYSTALS-Dilithium3 on record, War 50/0, Famine 50/0, Death Kyber-1024 on record, Corral 100/0, SIM-B Hypervisor 98/0, SIM-B Technician 98 with 3 vulnerable-crypto items flagged for drill-down.

Authorization: Leon GO (chat authorization, Oct 13, 2026, 13:51 CT) for the battery; Leon ACK (chat ack, Oct 13, 2026, 13:53 CT) for SIP-8 approval and standard publication. Two-key curation: Gabriel vet complete.
